messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: `CRITICAL - lb-targets-unhealthy-eu-prod` — 5xx spike & TLS handshake failures observed. Incident key: PDINC_84219. Auto-page to #incidents and on-call.
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: incident created (PDINC_84219). Notifying escalation policy: infra-oncall. https://pagerduty.example/PDINC_84219
mike_oncall: acked (mike_oncall) — taking it. quick triage: seeing increased 5xx from eu region in our synthetic checks. Starting timeline + customers impacted.
jess_prod: seeing customer reports: several EU customers get TLS handshake timeouts or 503s for /v1/generate and embeddings endpoints. Severity looks P1 (customer-facing).
rico_netops: I can see ALB target group `redwood-eu-api-tg` has 40% unhealthy targets in eu-west-1. Health checks failing with TLS handshake from the ALB to targets, not the client side (we're failing backend TLS).
evelyn_sre: logs show recent autoscale churn + kernel upgrade on the eu pool around 02:10 UTC. Could be connection limits exhausted during rolling nodes. Posting a sample error from router logs:

```
2026-03-14T02:11:02Z router[proxy-3]: upstream tls handshake error: remote error: tls: handshake failure
2026-03-14T02:11:03Z router[proxy-7]: connection reset by peer
```

mike_oncall: good catch. Any recent deploy/infra change? jess_prod?
jess_prod: we rolled a small LB routing policy change for canary domains at 01:55 UTC: reduced weight to eu by 20% and changed backend tls profile to `tlsv1.3-strict` for canary. Might be related if ALB/backend cert negotiation is impacted.
evelyn_sre: can we confirm if backend certs rotated? `kubectl get secret backend-tls -n prod-eu` shows unchanged. But node kernel update + sidecar envoy version mismatch could cause TLS handshake differences.
rico_netops: I'm going to temporarily remove unhealthy targets from rotation and divert traffic to eu-fallback pool. Will do weighted shift via Traffic Manager. Command:

```
trafficctl set-weight --route api.global --region eu-west-1 --weight 10
trafficctl set-weight --route api.global --region eu-fallback --weight 90
```

mike_oncall: do it and post result. Also enable enhanced logging for ALB health checks.
rico_netops: done. new weights applied. Health check spike reduced from 47% to 12% unhealthy within 45s. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: PDINC_84219 status: acknowledged by mike_oncall. Next escalation scheduled in 15m if unresolved.

jess_prod: customers still seeing TLS timeouts — probably because existing connections sticky to unhealthy targets. Suggest immediate plan: (1) shift traffic weights (done), (2) gracefully drain unhealthy targets, (3) scale up eu pool + postpone kernel upgrade on remaining nodes, (4) rollback canary tls-profile change if we see continued failures.

evelyn_sre: draining targets now:
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/redwood-eu-api-tg/abcd --targets Id=i-0a1b2c3d
```

mike_oncall: scaling eu pool + quick healthcheck: `ascli scale --pool eu-api --min 10 --desired 18` — started.

10m later

rico_netops: healthchecks down to 0% unhealthy. TLS handshake errors dropping. Synthetic hit rate for /v1/generate in eu is green.
jess_prod: still seeing intermittent 503s from a subset of customers behind CloudFront. Could be stale DNS caches pointing to IPs with unhealthy AZ. Any DNS changes recently?
evelyn_sre: no DNS pushes recently. But we did change ALB target weights; CDNs might have cached edge decisions. Suggest adding a short TTL for the edge canonical domain or force a purge for customers experiencing issues.

pm_zoe: compiling customer impact list. So far: 12 enterprise customers reported degraded response latency and some 503s between 01:55–02:40 UTC. No data exfiltration. Major customer-impact windows align with canary rollout + node upgrades.
mike_oncall: next step: rollback canary tls-profile change to `tlsv1.2-compatible` to see if handshake stabilizes. jess, can you patch the routing policy back?
jess_prod: rolling back now.

```
api-routerctl set-policy --domain canary.redwood.ai --tls-profile tlsv1.2-compatible --apply
```

jess_prod: rollback applied at 02:34 UTC.
evelyn_sre: monitoring: backend tls handshake errors reduced to baseline. ALB target group stable. Scaling completed, new instances healthy.

mike_oncall: starting verification run — run internal smoke tests and ask customer success to validate for impacted customers.

20m later

pm_zoe: customer outreach: CS sent targeted messages to the 12 affected accounts, offering SLA credits and a brief postmortem. They confirm API availability restored for all but one account which required local cache purge.
jess_prod: creating follow-up runbook items: avoid rolling kernel + TLS-profile changes simultaneously; add canary abort guard if ALB health > 5% unhealthy in 10m window; decrease default connection keepalive to 15s for eu pool.

mike_oncall: incident resolved -> monitoring for 2h. Summary for postmortem (short): root cause = simultaneous canary TLS-profile change + node kernel upgrades leading to TLS negotiation mismatch and transient connection exhaustion during autoscale. Mitigations = traffic weight shift, drain unhealthy targets, rollback tls-profile, scale up pool. Customer impact = degraded latency/503s for 12 customers in EU, no data loss.

incident-bot: Incident PDINC_84219 marked RESOLVED by mike_oncall at 02:58 UTC. Follow-up: postmortem assigned to jess_prod, rico_netops, and evelyn_sre. Due in 48h.

mike_oncall: thumbs for handoff. tagging follow-ups:
- jess_prod: prepare postmortem draft (include timeline, deploy + infra overlap)
- rico_netops: propose improved health-check thresholds and automated weight-shift playbook
- evelyn_sre: test rolling node upgrades against tls-profile permutations in staging

pm_zoe: adding customer impact note and CS summary to the ticket. Will coordinate postmortem review with stakeholders.

mike_oncall: closing thread here. Thanks everyone :heart:
